entry.title: STO with Handling Units via MIGO
entry.content:
Hi Dear Experts,

 
We currently have a standard STO process with outbound delivery, Handling Units (HUs), PGI, and automatic inbound delivery creation via SPED for some plants. In that process, the HUs are transferred to the receiving plant successfully.
 
However, enabling the same SPED-based process for additional plants would require considerable business and customization effort.
 
Therefore, I am looking for an alternative approach.
 
Current requirement:
 
1. Create STO
2. Create outbound delivery and pack HUs
3. Post Goods Issue (PGI)
4. User performs Goods Receipt in MIGO via Handling Units with reference to the STO/outbound process
5. The same HUs should become available in the receiving plant automatically

 

The goal is to keep the user process as simple as possible (only MIGO) and avoid introducing a full SPED/inbound delivery rollout for these plants.
 
I have already tested some cases and made some configs but couldnt get proper solution. I had encountered HID-Inbnd Dlv. HU Mvmnt delivery type but couldnt trigger that. I think it is used in VLMOVE processes but need to clarify.
If I use VLMOVE to move that handling units to the another plant, so what will happen to outbound delivery, how can I post goods issue with hand.units as well? 
 
Has anyone implemented a similar scenario?
 
- Is there a standard way to transfer HU information during MIGO GR without a manually or SPED-created inbound delivery?
- Can an inbound delivery be created automatically in the background only for HU continuity?
- Are there any standard HU-managed STO processes that allow HU reuse in the receiving plant without the full SPED setup?
 
 
Kind regards,
Nedim Yilmaz

entry.title: Incorrect delivery status showing in VBUK table
entry.content:
Hi all,

We use batch determination based on a Customer-Material freshness requirement. If freshness is maintained as 70%, only batches with freshness ≥70% should be selected during delivery creation.

Stock:

Batch 1: 75% freshness, Qty 2
Batch 2: 50% freshness, Qty 5
Batch 3: 60% freshness, Qty 5

A sales order is created for Qty 4.

Case 1

Delivery is created with proposed Qty 4.
Batch determination finds only Qty 2 from Batch 1 (eligible batch).
After saving, delivery quantity is automatically reduced to Qty 2.
Sales order header shows "Partially Delivered".
However, table (VBUK) level status is updated as "Delivery Completed".

Later, new stock arrives:

Batch 4: 80% freshness, Qty 5

When creating the next delivery, the system issues: "No delivery-relevant items in order xxx"

The remaining Qty 2 is not considered for delivery, although eligible stock exists.

Case 2

If delivery quantity is manually changed from Qty 4 to Qty 2 before saving the first delivery, item status remains "Partially Delivered".
A second delivery can then be created successfully using Batch 4.

Question: Why is the Table (VBUK) level being marked as "Delivery Completed" in Case 1 when only Qty 2 of Qty 4 is delivered? Which status/update logic controls this behavior, and how can it be corrected so that subsequent deliveries can be created when eligible stock becomes available later?

Thanks,
Nimmala Prasanthkumar.

entry.title: Product Group Not Populated in Manage Sales Prices - Preventing Filtering of Sales Price Records
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

We are working with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Retail) and have a question regarding the Manage Prices - Sales application.

In our system, the Product Group field is available in the sales price records but remains empty.

Our business users would like to use this field as a filter when reviewing sales prices. In our business process, the Product Group is used to represent the product brand.

We have verified that the products are assigned to Product Groups in the product master data; however, this information does not appear in the corresponding sales price records displayed in Manage Prices - Sales.

Could you please clarify:

  1. How is the Product Group field in Manage Prices - Sales determined?
  2. Is the value expected to be derived from Product Master data?
  3. Is Product Group supported as a filter only in specific pricing scenarios?
  4. Is the field expected to be populated for material-based sales price records?
  5. Is the current behavior standard, or is additional configuration required?

Our objective is not to create price conditions by Product Group. We only need to display and filter sales price records by the Product Group (brand) assigned to the products.

Any guidance would be appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: Issue in creating credit memo request (CR)
entry.content:
We are currently facing an issue while creating Credit Memo Requests for a few materials in the PRD system.

However, for the same material, customer, and sales area combination, we are able to create Sales Orders (OR), Returns, and other sales documents without any issues. The following checks have already been performed:

Checked the relevant Item Category determination and configuration.
Performed a comparison between working and non-working material/customer combinations, but no obvious differences were found.

Could you please help us identify the root cause of this issue?

entry.title: Unwanted Foreign trade data number while Credit memo creation
entry.content:
• I am facing an issue where a Foreign Trade Data Number (vbrk-exnum) is unexpectedly generated during the creation of an order-related Credit Memo (referenced from a Credit Memo without quantity request).

  • The transaction is purely domestic, with the physical Departure and Destination countries being exactly the same.

  • Master data checks via KNA1 confirm that the assigned countries for the Sold-To, Ship-To, and Payer partners all match this single country.

  • In the Copy Control (VTFA) configuration, the header setting for Determ.export data is set to 'B' (Redetermine export data).

  • I have checked tables EIKP, LIKP, VBRK, and VBRP and verified that previous documents in this specific flow, such as the Delivery and Invoice, did not have a Foreign Trade Data Number generated.

  • Crucially, the Export Indicator (EXPKZ) is completely blank for all documents across the entire document flow.

  • Because EXPKZ is blank, standard SAP logic (FORM EXPORT_DATEN_ERMITTELN) should normally bypass the generation of foreign trade data.

  • We are looking to find out if there are any standard user exits, BAdIs, or inherent copy control behaviors (specifically related to Determ.export data = 'B') that would interfere here and force the EXNUM generation despite the domestic setup and blank indicator.

    Please help me find some solution to this

entry.title: Valuation of Stock in Transit for Previous-Period Postings (KBA 3449848)
entry.content:
We would like to complete the entire process within the previous posting period, including sales order creation, goods issue posting to transfer stock to valuated Stock in Transit (SiT), and the final goods issue upon Proof of Delivery (POD) confirmation.

However, according to SAP KBA 3449848, SiT stock is valuated using the standard price of the current period, even when the goods movement is posted to the previous period.

Is it possible to complete the entire process, including the final goods issue upon POD confirmation, using the standard price of the previous period?

If not, is this behavior a standard SAP system limitation, or is there any configuration or alternative approach that would allow us to use the previous period's standard price?

entry.title: Single Material for Sales Order Stock (E) and Project Stock (Q)
entry.content:
Dear SAP Experts,

I need your advice on the following scenario in SAP S/4HANA 2025 Private Cloud.

My client is an asphalt manufacturing company. They produce the same asphalt product for two purposes:

  1. Internal Project Consumption: Asphalt is produced and consumed in internal construction projects using Project Stock (Special Stock Q), valuated against the respective WBS element.

  2. External Customer Sales: Asphalt is produced against customer orders using Make-to-Order (MTO), with Sales Order Stock (Special Stock E).

Both scenarios use the same material code.

My Questions:

  1. Is it possible to manage the same material under both Special Stock E and Q?

  2. Can SAP determine different requirements types dynamically based on the business process (Sales Order vs. WBS)?

  3. Can this be achieved through standard configuration without creating separate material codes?

  4. What is the recommended best-practice approach?

I would appreciate your suggestions and guidance on the standard SAP solution.

Thank you.

silambarasan R
